alice.le: heads up — the starter sample app fails in the edge runner when package.json has \"type\": \"module\" and we import the SDK as commonjs. stack trace points at runtime module loader.
ben_rm: repro? iirc the sdk ships both cjs + esm entries, but tsconfig + bundler can pick the wrong one for the edge target.
alice.le: minimal repro in the sample: run `npm init -y && npm i @redwood/inference-sdk` then create `index.ts` with `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'` and `tsc && esbuild` -> runtime: \"Unexpected token 'export'\" in the edge sandbox.
carol-ux: sounds like module resolution mismatch. what's tsconfig module/target? also do you have `package.json` \"type\": \"module\"? edge bundlers often set \"module\": \"esnext\".
alice.le: tsconfig is pretty standard: \"module\": \"esnext\", \"target\": \"es2020\", \"moduleResolution\": \"node\". package.json has \"type\": \"module\" because other teams using ESM. But our CI builds for node (cjs) and edge (esm) separately.
ben_rm: common pitfall: node's default resolution picks the esm entry when \"type\": \"module\". SDK's cjs export is still there but bundler may inline ESM-only code paths that use `export default` which Edge runtime doesn't accept when transpiled incorrectly.
alice.le: would switching moduleResolution to \"node16\" or adding `package.json` exports map help? i tried adding `\"exports\": { \".\": {\"import\": \"dist/esm/index.js\", \"require\": \"dist/cjs/index.js\"}}` but the edge runner still pulled esm.
carol-ux: export map is correct in principle. edge bundlers sometimes prefer the import condition; but if your final bundle contains raw `export` tokens it's likely esbuild target config is wrong. what does your esbuild target/bundle format look like?
alice.le: esbuild config: `format: 'iife', target: 'es2020', platform: 'browser'` — building for edge. but the emitted bundle contained `export` in one module wrapper, so the runtime threw.
ben_rm: try `format: 'esm'` for edge builds and let the runner use native ESM. or force esbuild to bundle the sdk entry point into the final file so no runtime import resolution is needed. also ensure `tsconfig.compilerOptions.module: 'esnext'` for emit and let esbuild handle transformation.
alice.le: ok will try. another thing: typings are weird — our sample's `RedwoodClient` overloads are ambiguous in TS when using `unknown` vs `any` in the retry helper. Consumers see `TS2345` when passing the auth token type.
carol-ux: can you paste the snippet? maybe we should tighten overloads or prefer a single generic with constraint.
alice.le: snippet:
```
function call<T = any>(opts: CallOptions<T>): Promise<T>
function call(opts: CallOptions<any>) { /* ... */ }
```
TS complains when callers do `client.call<{foo:string}>({})` vs `client.call({})` without generics — inference collapses because of the `any` fallback.
ben_rm: that's classic. prefer `unknown` for the default generic and then `type Guard<T> = T extends unknown ? T : never`? jk. more practically: use a single generic with `T = unknown` and use proper assertions in the implementation. overloads with `any` as fallback kill inference.
carol-ux: also the auth/retry layer currently wraps responses with `.then()` that erases generics in the chain — type is widened to `any` there. we need to keep generics through the wrapper, e.g., `function withRetry<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T>`.
alice.le: good call. I'll open a tiny PR to change the public signature to `Promise<T>` in retry wrapper. will that be a breaking change?
ben_rm: shouldn't be if we keep implementation compatible. but update our d.ts exports and add a test that forces inference in TS (we have a `tsd` harness). add a test case for `client.call<{id:number}>` to ensure the return type is inferred.
carol-ux: while at it, can we add a small note in the sample app README about `package.json` \"type\" effects and esbuild settings for edge vs node? new users keep tripping on that.
alice.le: yes i'll add README note and a checklist: (1) pick bundle format (esm vs iife) (2) set esbuild target+platform (3) ensure exports map exists if you need dual packages (4) tsconfig moduleResolution node16 for consistency.
deploy-bot: deployment queued for sample-app-fix branch — status: pending
ben_rm: thanks. last micro-quirk: default `tsconfig` in the starter uses `skipLibCheck: false` which surfaces a noisy overload mismatch from the SDK d.ts because of our legacy overload definitions. maybe set `skipLibCheck: true` in starter to reduce friction until we ship the typing cleanup.
carol-ux: agreed. but we should fix the SDK d.ts too. added to infra board.
alice.le: i'll make the PRs: (a) fix retry wrapper generics, (b) update sample README + esbuild example, (c) set skipLibCheck in starter template. pinging @ben_rm for review.
ben_rm: ack. thanks for catching — this was causing a few internal eng teams to file onboarding tickets. :pray:
carol-ux: nice triage. small follow-ups: add a note in the changelog about the typing improvements and a migration note for teams that use explicit `any` generics.
alice.le: will do — sending PRs shortly.
